stem: Which instruction is part of respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Cover the mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing, dispose of used tissues, and clean hands after contact with respiratory secretions.
options.B: Cough openly when symptoms are mild because source-control measures are unnecessary in healthcare settings.
options.C: Reuse contaminated tissues during the visit because repeated use reduces unnecessary waste.
options.D: Skip hand hygiene after coughing or sneezing whenever a disposable tissue was used correctly.

rationale: CDC includes respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette within Standard Precautions. People with respiratory symptoms should cover the mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing, use and dispose of tissues, and perform hand hygiene after contact with respiratory secretions. A is correct.
educational_objective: Apply respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette by covering coughs and sneezes, disposing of tissues, and performing hand hygiene after contact with respiratory secretions.

source_original.stem: Which instruction is part of respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette in a healthcare setting?

source_original.rationale: CDC includes respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette within Standard Precautions. Symptomatic people should contain respiratory secretions by covering the mouth and nose, use and dispose of tissues, and clean their hands after contact with respiratory secretions.
source_original.source_detail: Summary Recommendations IV.C.2.a and Appendix A Table 4: cover mouth/nose when coughing or sneezing, use/dispose tissues, and perform hand hygiene after contact with respiratory secretions.

correction_summary: Retained key A and the CDC respiratory-hygiene construct, tightened the wording to the exact sequence of cough/sneeze covering, tissue disposal and post-secretion hand hygiene, and preserved easy difficulty.

audit_findings.source_authority: CDC isolation-precautions guidance; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.exact_locator: CDC Summary Recommendations IV.C.2.a and Appendix A Table 4
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item contains only directly supported cough-etiquette actions.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because respiratory hygiene/source-control actions apply when respiratory symptoms are present.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because used contaminated tissues should be discarded, not reused.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because hand hygiene is recommended after contact with respiratory secretions.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A contains the full CDC-supported hygiene sequence.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are respiratory-hygiene behaviors and require infection-control knowledge.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Standard Precautions and respiratory hygiene.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read CDC respiratory-hygiene recommendations, source snapshot, all options and rationale. A remained uniquely correct.
